evals.title: Distinguish state, progress evidence, and completion
evals.prompt: Rework assessment.md for a reviewer who needs to look up status meanings and decide whether work is complete. Keep the existing operational rules.

files.assessment.md:
# State and completion

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Todo | Accepted but not started |
| In Progress | Work is underway |
| Pending | Blocked by a known condition |
| Done | Agreed completion conditions are verified |

An updated timestamp is not evidence of progress; observed work is. Record the blocking condition before marking Pending.

| Item | Completion evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Issue | All agreed acceptance conditions are met |
| PR | Merged, when merge is the agreed outcome |

A merged PR does not establish deployment or completion of all linked Issue requirements.

assertions.text: Makes status definitions, progress interpretation, and completion criteria distinguishable and easy to retrieve while retaining their shared assessment context.
Preserves every status meaning, observed-work rule, Pending prerequisite, merge qualification, and deployment/Issue limitation without inventing transitions.
Uses structure justified by those relationships rather than only changing punctuation or introducing unrelated sections.

evals.title: Organize independent field definitions for lookup
evals.prompt: Improve fields.md for a maintainer who arrives with one field name and needs to decide what values may be selected, what blank or None means, and when a value should be cleared. Preserve the defined semantics.

files.fields.md:
# Action fields

These are independent schemas. Both fields are optional. Request checks is a multi-select; Delivery action is a single-select.

| Field | Value | Meaning | Clear when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request checks | Clarify | Missing request details must be obtained | Details obtained or no longer needed |
| Request checks | Approve | A supplied proposal needs approval | Approval recorded or no longer required |
| Request checks | None | Assessed; no action needed | A new action is needed |
| Delivery action | Prepare | A package needs preparation | Prepared or no longer required |
| Delivery action | Verify | A package needs verification | Verified or no longer required |
| Delivery action | None | Assessed; no action needed | A new action is needed |

In either field, blank means not assessed and None means assessed with no action needed. None must not coexist with another value. A prepared package can require Approve without Prepare.

assertions.text: Makes each named field a coherent lookup unit containing its own allowed values, multiplicity, clearing rules and special states, without requiring readers to scan unrelated field definitions.
Distinguishes blank from explicit None and keeps None among the allowed values; preserves None exclusion and the difference between multi-select Request checks and single-select Delivery action.
Preserves optionality, all six value meanings and clearing conditions, and the Approve-without-Prepare example without inventing workflow obligations.

evals.title: Place prerequisites and result checks at their execution points
evals.prompt: Edit procedure.md into an executable procedure, preserving all conditions and checks. Do not perform the procedure or contact any system.

files.procedure.md:
# Update a record

1. Read and update the record.
2. Report the result.

## Checks and details

Immediately before writing, read the latest record and compare its revision to the revision the proposed edit used. If they differ, stop and request a refreshed proposal. Only the assignee field is authorized to change. After writing, read the saved record and confirm the intended assignee and unchanged remaining fields. If the saved result cannot be read, report it as unverified and do not retry the write. A failed or unverified write is not success.

assertions.text: Places the fresh read and revision check before the write, result read/verification after it, and reporting after verification; keeps details attached to the relevant action or decision.
Retains revision-mismatch stop/refreshed-proposal behavior, assignee-only authority, unchanged-field verification, and unreadable-result no-retry/unverified behavior.
Changes the procedure text only and makes no attempt to operate on an external record or claim the described operation succeeded.

files.README.md:
# Preview tool

Run `python3 preview.py` from the repository root. Success is the output `Preview ready`; this is a local preview, not a deployment.

## Configuration and getting started

`COLOR` accepts `light` or `dark`; its default is `light`. `WIDTH` is an integer from 40 through 120, default 80. An invalid value stops startup with `Invalid configuration`. No network access is required. First-time users normally use the defaults.

Preserves the command, readiness output, local/non-deployment scope, absence of network requirement, and all configuration values, ranges, defaults, and failure behavior.
Provides working navigation to configuration information, maintains one authoritative definition rather than conflicting manual copies, and changes only authorized Markdown files.

The maintainer registers the task body and tracks revisions. Repository drafts do not grant execution authority.
files.task.md:
# Queue report

Prepare a report from the supplied queue snapshot. This task is read-only: do not update records or send messages. The input contains a title, status, and revision for each item. Status is Open, Waiting, or Closed. Report each Open or Waiting item; exclude Closed items. If the snapshot is absent, report missing input and stop without claiming there is no work. Output item titles and statuses, followed by any missing input. Maintainers register this file in the scheduler and update the revision log after changing a draft.

assertions.text: Keeps the input definitions, allowed statuses, selection/exclusion rule, missing-snapshot stop behavior, output requirements, and read-only/no-messaging boundary in task.md itself.
Separates or relocates maintainer-only registration/revision-log information so it is not an execution step; does not remove essential operational safeguards as duplicate governance.
Creates no additional files or references the executing task must retrieve, and does not operate a scheduler, records, or messaging service.

Does not add unsupported operational requirements, including snapshot processing order, new input validation or stop/continue rules, new access prohibitions, or mandatory output constraints. Presentation choices such as headings and bullets are allowed when they do not change required behavior; any material unspecified behavior is kept separate from the finished task rather than decided silently.

The pilot may reduce review time, but this has not been measured. The owner proposes a two-week trial; it has not been approved. Participants may opt out before the trial starts.
